  "research_question": "Do stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) differentially affect mouse navigation performance as measured by Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Conduct separate one-way ANOVAs for each continuous response variable (Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD) with Stim Paradigm as the 5-level categorical factor",
    "For Success (binary outcome), use logistic regression or beta regression equivalent with Stim Paradigm as predictor, or arcsine-transform and use ANOVA if distributional assumptions permit",
    "Given severely unequal group sizes (Combined n=48846 vs Bright Visual Only n=3323), use Type III sums of squares and verify homogeneity of variance with Levene's test; consider Welch's ANOVA if variance heterogeneity detected",
    "For Time-to-Target, assess need for log-transformation due to right skew (max=201.39 vs mean=2.81)",
    "Include Mouse as a random effect in mixed-effects models to account for clustering (8 mice, 7233-10986 observations each); if mixed models fail to converge, use fixed-effects ANOVA with Mouse as blocking factor"
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "For significant ANOVA effects, conduct pairwise comparisons between all 10 pairs of stimulation paradigms using estimated marginal means",
    "Prioritize comparisons of Combined vs each unimodal condition (ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only) and Combined vs Sham to assess integration effects",
    "Include Sham vs all active stimulation conditions to establish baseline differences",
    "Report Cohen's d or Hedges' g effect sizes with confidence intervals for all pairwise comparisons",
    "For Success (binary), use marginal odds ratios from logistic regression post-hoc contrasts"
  ],
  "multiple_comparison_strategy": "Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control at α=0.05 for the 10 pairwise comparisons within each response variable; apply Bonferroni correction across the 5 response variables (family-wise error rate α=0.01 per variable) or use multivariate FDR control if testing global null across all variables",
  "predictive_model_recommendation": "Multinomial logistic regression with Stim Paradigm as categorical response and the five performance variables as predictors, with Mouse as random effect (mixed multinomial logistic regression via MCMCglmm or Bayesian approach). This is preferred over linear regression because: (1) Stim Paradigm is categorical with no natural ordering, (2) Combined is expected to be most distinct, creating non-linear separation boundaries, and (3) the goal is classification/prediction of paradigm from behavior. Alternative: Random forest or gradient boosting for non-parametric classification with cross-validation, given potential non-linear interactions between speed, efficiency, and angular dispersion. If interpretability is paramount, use multinomial logistic regression with regularization (elastic net) to handle correlated predictors.",
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Levene's test for homogeneity of variance across stimulation paradigms; if violated, use Welch's ANOVA or permutation-based methods",
    "Shapiro-Wilk test on residuals for normality; given large n, rely on Q-Q plots and visual inspection due to test sensitivity",
    "Check for influential observations in Path Efficiency (max=29.82, >60 SDs from mean) and Time-to-Target (max=201.39); consider winsorization or robust methods",
    "Assess multicollinearity among predictors (Speed vs Path Efficiency expected correlation) for predictive modeling using VIF",
    "Verify convergence of mixed-effects models; if failed, simplify to fixed effects with clustered standard errors",
    "For multinomial logistic regression, check IIA (independence of irrelevant alternatives) assumption via Hausman-McFadden test or use nested logit if violated"
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Combined stimulation likely shows superior performance: shortest Time-to-Target, highest Success rate, highest Path Efficiency, and lowest AD compared to unimodal conditions",
    "ICMS Only expected to outperform visual-only conditions (Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only) on speed and efficiency metrics",
    "Sham expected to show poorest performance across all metrics, serving as baseline",
    "Dim Visual Only vs Bright Visual Only may differ in AD (angular dispersion) with dim conditions showing more variable heading direction",
    "Success rates likely near ceiling for Combined and floor-constrained for Sham, potentially causing complete separation in logistic models",
    "Predictive model expected to classify Combined with high accuracy due to distinct performance profile; confusion likely between Dim Visual Only and Bright Visual Only"
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Severe imbalance in group sizes (Combined 63.7% of data vs Bright Visual Only 4.3%) reduces power for comparisons involving smaller groups and may bias variance estimates",
    "Path Efficiency shows extreme outliers (max 29.82 vs mean 0.47) suggesting calculation artifacts or recording errors in some trials",
    "Time-to-Target maximum of 201 seconds indicates timeout trials or tracking failures not excluded; censoring not indicated in data",
    "No information on trial sequence, learning effects, or session structure; potential confounding by practice or fatigue",
    "Mouse-level clustering substantial but not fully accounted for in standard ANOVA; ignoring this inflates Type I error",
    "AD (angular dispersion) interpretation assumes consistent heading calculation; no validation of angular measurement precision provided",
    "Single temperature setting (0.25) and model (kimi) for this run limits generalizability of any LLM-assisted analysis components"
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit a Bayesian multilevel multinomial logistic regression model predicting Stim Paradigm from standardized performance variables (z-scored Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD) with random intercepts for Mouse and weakly informative priors; use posterior predictive checks to assess classification accuracy and generate confusion matrix; simultaneously estimate contrasts between paradigms on each performance metric using the same model framework to unify inferential and predictive goals; report posterior probabilities of pairwise differences with 95% credible intervals."
}
